{{Short description|German biochemist}}
'''Alfred "Fred" Wittinghofer''' (born 23 May 1943) is a German biochemist.

==Education and career==
At [[RWTH Aachen University]] he studied chemistry from 1963 with ''[[Diplom]]'' in 1968 and with doctorate ([[Promotion (Germany)|''Promotion'']]) in 1971. His doctoral work was done at RWTH Aachen University's ''Deutsches Wollforschungsinstitut'' (now called the {{ill|DWI – Leibniz-Institut für Interaktive Materialien|de}}). He worked from 1971 to 1973 as a postdoc at the [[University of North Carolina]]. At Heidelberg's [[Max Planck Institute for Medical Research]] he was 1974 from 1979 a scientific assistant and 1980 from 1993 a research group leader. In 1992 he completed his [[habilitation]] in biochemistry at the University of Heidelberg. At Dortmund's [[Max Planck Institute for Molecular Physiology]], he was from 1993 to 2009 director of the structural biology department and from 2009 to 2016 "Emeritus Scientific Member" of the institute. From 1994 to 2009 he was [[Academic ranks in Germany#Other positions|''Honorarprofessor'']] for biochemistry at the [[Ruhr University Bochum]].<ref name=Leopoldina>{{cite web|title=Prof. Dr. Alfred Wittinghofer|website=List of Members, Leopoldina Nationale Akademie der Wissenschafter|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/alfred-wittinghofer/}}</ref><ref name=AcademiaEuropaea>{{cite web|title=Alfred Wittinghofer|website=Academia Europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Wittinghofer_Alfred}}</ref>

Wittinghofer and colleagues examined the structure, function and mode of action of the [[oncogene]] product [[Ras (protein)|Ras]].<ref name=Louis-Jeantet>{{cite web|title=Professor Alfred Wittinghofer, Winner of the 2001 Louis-Jeantet Prize for medicine|website=Fondation Louis-Jeantet|date=October 2017|url=https://www.jeantet.ch/en/prix-louis-jeantet/laureats/2001-en/professeur-alfred-wittinghofer/}} (in French)</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Alfred Wittinghofer, Max Planck Institute of Molecular Physiology|website=iBiology|url=https://www.ibiology.org/speakers/alfred-wittinghofer/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Alfred Wittinghofer, PhD|website=The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research|url=https://www.michaeljfox.org/researcher/alfred-wittinghofer-phd}}</ref>

He has received at least a dozen honors and awards. He was elected in 1995 a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization|European Molecular Biology Organization (EMBO)]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Alfred Wittinghofer|website=EMBO (embo.org)|url=https://people.embo.org/profile/alfred-wittinghofer}}</ref> and in 2001 a member of both [[Academia Europaea]]<ref name=AcademiaEuropaea/> and the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref name=Leopoldina/> He was awarded in 2001 the [[Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]],<ref name=Louis-Jeantet/> in 2003 the [[Otto Warburg Medal]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://idw-online.de/pages/de/news71505|date=3 November 2003|title=Otto Warburg Medaille an Prof. Alfred Wittinghofer|website=idw — Informationsdienst Wissenschaft}}</ref> and in 2019 the STS Honorary Medal from the Signal Transduction Society/Gesellschaft für Signaltransduktion and the ''[[International Journal of Molecular Sciences]]''.<ref>{{cite web|date=12 December 2019|title=Professor Alfred Wittinghofer Awarded the STS Medal by the STS and IJMS|website=MDPI (Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute)|url=https://www.mdpi.com/about/announcements/1741}}</ref>
